newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: China may join W.Australian iron processing plant.
newsitem.headline: China may join W.Australian iron processing plant.

text.p: China could participate in a major new iron processing plant in Western Australia (WA), Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday.

A Chinese industry group would arrive in Australia in July this year to conduct a feasibility study into a direct reduced iron (DRI) process that could open an export market of A$500 million a year and create 2,000 jobs, Howard said in a radio interview from Beijing.
The process would involve the use of large volumes of liquified natural gas, he said.
Howard said Chinese premier Li Peng had agreed to an Australian proposal to examine Chinese participation in the new plant.
The plan, being developed by three companies in Australia, could generate A$1 billion in additional investment, he said, but did not name the project involved.
Several large-scale projects are being promoted in Western Australia for the production of DRI or hot briquetted iron (HBI), to be used as feedstock in electric arc furnace steelmaking.

The two front-runners are Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), with its A$1.5 billion HBI plant, and privately-held Australian United Steel Industry Ltd (AUSI Ltd), which is developing a A$1.9 billion DRI plant.
AUSI chairman Sir Russel Madigan is presently travelling with Howard in China. Other company officers in Australia declined comment pending Madigan's return.

The AUSI proposal is based on the supply of iron ore from Hamersley Iron Pty Ltd's Parabadoo mine in WA and is scheduled to come on stream early in year 2000 at four million tonnes of DRI pellets a year, with full production by early 2001.
Hamersley is a unit of RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
This project, to be constructed at Mt Ankatel on the northwest coast of WA, plans to draw natural gas from a number of gas projects on the Northwest Shelf.

It is being promoted by Sir Russel Madigan, a leading figure in the development of Australia's iron ore industry, and other former top executives of the former CRA Ltd group. Last year Norwegian construction group Kvaerner ASA entered the project as equity partner.

BHP is building a A$1.5 billion HBI plant at Port Hedland in WA, with commissioning of the 2.5 million tonnes a year first stage set for mid-1998 and with plans for a A$1 billion second stage to increase capacity to either 3.75 million tonnes or five million tonnes.
BHP recently deferred building the second stage for at least two years, until commissioning of stage one, because of demands on group resources.

Other groups involved in WA DRI or iron ore enrichment plant plans include CRA, with its HIsmelt proposal for WA, Taiwanese-owned An Feng (Australia) Pty Ltd in conjunction with Australia's Kingstream Resources NL, the Mount Gibson consortium which involves German, U.S. and Australian interests, the privately-owned Mineralogy group.
The South Australian government also has a pig iron export plant proposal in train in conjunction with the Meekatharra Minerals Ltd group.
